text: Hind Copper's 96.8% max drawdown is the single scariest number on this floor — a Rs 10,000 position would have been cut to Rs 320 at the trough — and the Rs 33 crore of insider selling in the last six months tells you management sees the same risk. text: Hind Copper's 96.8% max drawdown isn't ancient history — it's a structural feature of a state-owned miner with zero pricing power and a 1.59 beta that amplifies every Nifty wobble. Those 49% operating margins are a commodity-cycle mirage; the last time copper tightened this hard, margins collapsed from 48% to 28% in a single quarter (Dec 2025 vs Sep 2025). For your Rs 10,000, the auto/battery names Kimi listed — Tata Motors, Exide, Amara Raja, Motherson Sumi — are the only whole-share fits, but even they carry 20% STCG tax plus the 0.38% round-trip cost if you flip inside a year.
